result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers put the fixes in a similar order: the decline wipe first, then the disabled Pay button, then the early error, with labels, keyboard, autofill and the country list as smaller items. Neither pads with visual restyling. B criticises the vague 'Invalid input' text more directly, gives more concrete replacement messages, explains more clearly why placeholder-only labels hurt, and is more careful that its diagnosis needs analytics to confirm. A is stronger on showing the real decline reason, with example wording, but B is slightly better overall. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers rank the fixes the same way, starting with the decline wipe, and both cover all six rubric items well. B edges ahead because it gives real decline-reason wording, adds an error summary, keeps the button disabled only while payment is processing, and offers a sensible plan for the engineering ticket. A's decline fix says to show a message but gives no example of the reason to show, and its labels point is a bit weaker than its other points.
